title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Writings destroyed — figure/type/sign language under pressure; yet adhered to truth
pass_a_gloss: Indeed, what precisely this most excellent Confessor’s modes of speaking concerning the Sacred Supper were is not so easy to decide, because this Man’s Writings were utterly suppressed and deleted by the numerous crowd of his enemies; What is more, it can be granted that this very Berengar, by the importunity of Transubstantiators already in that age raising their crests, was driven by zeal to such a point that commenting on the Sacred Supper he more often injected mention of Figure and Type and Sign than of the Antitype and Body of Christ most present in the same to all communicating Faithful; meanwhile it must at the same time be confessed that he firmly adhered to the truth as to the thing and substance, even if through his adversaries’ inhumanity he sometimes seems to have suffered something human.
pass_b_english: His exact modes of speaking on the Sacred Supper are hard to pin down: enemies thoroughly suppressed and deleted his writings.

Under Transubstantiators’ pressure he more often stressed Figure, Type, and Sign than Antitype and Christ’s most-present Body — yet as to the thing and substance he firmly held the truth, even if adversaries’ cruelty sometimes made him look merely human.
source_text: Equidem, quinam præcisè hujus præstantissimi Confessoris de Sacra Cœna loquendi modi fuerint, non adeò in proclivi est decernere, quod Scripta hujus Viri, ab inimicorum suorum numerosa turba, penitus oppressa deletaque sunt; Quid quòd, concedi potest, hunc ipsum Berengarium, Transsubstantiatorum, unô alioque jam tum seculo cristas erigentium, importunitate, eò zeli adactum fuisse, ut de S. Cœna commentatus, Figuræ crebrius Typique & Signi, quam Antitypi Corporisque Christi, in eadem, omnibus Fidelibus communicantibus præsentissimi, mentionem injecerit; interim fatendum insimul est, veritati, quà rem & substantiam, firmiter adhæsisse eum, etiamsi per inhumanitatem adversariorum suorum, aliquando passus aliquid humani videatur.
